full_judgment:
This Rule by the petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-1-1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. Natore in Title Appeal No. 124 of 1989 reversing those dated 30-5-89 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Na tore in Other Class suit No.112 of 1979. 

 2. The opposite party as plaintiff filed the OC suit No.112 of 1979 against the present petitioner for declaration of his title to the suit land and recovery of possession therein stating that the suit land originally belonged to Yakub Ali Khalifa and Ishahaq Ali purchased the land from Yakub Ali. Thereafter the opposite party purchased the same from Ishahaq Ali. Petitioner has been residing in the suit land on permission of Yakub Ali. The petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement stating that the purchase deed of Ishaque from Yakub Ali was forged and that the petitioner had been possessing the suit land including other lands by constructing house thereon. The learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 30-5-1989. Plaintiff preferred appeal and the appeal was allowed and the suit was decreed by the learned Subordinate Judge by impugned judgment and decree dated 31-1-91. The another story of case is that, the suit was first dismissed by the learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 30-12-1981 and against that judgment and decree plaintiff preferred appeal before the learned District Judge being Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984. The learned District Judge disposed of the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 9-1-1986 allowing the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and sent the suit back on remand for fresh trial in accordance with law and in the light of the observation made in the body of the judgment. In the body of the judgment the learned District Judge observed that the vendor of the plaintiff-appellant and defendant-respondent inherited the suit property from Yakub All and plaintiff''s father, and in the circumstances it is proper and for ends of justice the plaintiff appellant should be given opportunity to amend the plaint suitably for the partition of share instead of khash possession. so that he may get relief in the suit. After receiving the suit on remand the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on 30-5-89 with the observation that all the co-sharers of the suit land are not made parties to the suit and according to the direction of the appellate Court suit was not made a partition suit after amendment when plaintiff preferred appeal and the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 31-1-1991 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved at the aforesaid judgment and decree the present application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is preferred by the petitioner and obtained the Rule. 

 3. Mr A K M Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the plaintiff did not comply with the direction of appellate Court for amending the suit and make it a partition suit and on this ground trial Court has rightly dismissed the suit. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge in his impugned judgment did not discuss the question of amendment of the suit as directed in previous first appeal of the suit or discard the observation of the learned Assistant Judge made on this point and that he gave a new judgment considering the evidence on record and, as such, his judgment is not tenable in law. In support of the above contention he relied on a decision reported in AIR 1957 (Patna) 534, wherein their Lordships held that, the decision of the appellate Court before remand on other question must be deemed to have been finally decided by the remand order, and as such, it was not open to his successor who was a court of co-ordinate jurisdiction, on an appeal on the second occasion against the decree of remand, to go behind that finding and to come to a contrary finding. He also relied on another decision of similar nature reported in AIR 1975. 

 4. In reply to the above contention Dr Rafiqur Rahman submits that the plaintiff respondent made two amendments after remand of the suit and, as such, the submission in support of his case law reported in AIR 1957, as stated above and submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is not applicable. He brought to my notice the lower court's record wherein he showed that by order dated 16-4-1988, plaintiff has already amended the suit. I have gone through the record. It is found that plaintiff amended the plaint twice by order dated 16-4-1988. Plaintiff amended the area of the suit land by inserting 4½ decimal land in place of 3 decimal land and value Taka 7,000.00 in place of 400.00. By amendment dated 14-1-1987 the plaintiff amended some statements of the plaint. But no such amendment is made as directed by the learned District Judge in previous appeal No.98 of 1984 of the present suit. When the appellate Court after due consideration and for the ends of justice gave opportunity to a party to amend the suit and change the nature of the suit it became obligatory to the party to do the same unless the party being aggrieved at preferred revision against such observation. In the instant case the plaintiff appellant did not comply with direction of appellate Court. So, the learned Assistant Judge rightly dismissed the suit. But learned Subordinate Judge on appeal without discarding the observation of the trial Court set aside the judgment and decreed the suit after discussing the evidence independently as trial Court and not as an appellate Court. So, the judgment of the appellate Court can not be considered as passed on due consideration and discarding the observation made by the learned Assistant Judge on the basis of the judgment of the First Appeal No. 98 of 1984. In view of above discussion I find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
